source_text:
Ὑμεῖς μὲν οὖν ἠξιώσατε διὰ πλειόνων δηλωθῆναι ὑμῖν τὰ γενόμενα, ἡμεῖς δὲ κατὰ τὸ παρὸν ἐπὶ κεφαλαίῳ μεμηνύκαμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ ἡμῶν Μαρκίωνος. μαθόντες οὖν ταῦτα καὶ τοῖς ἐπέκεινα ἀδελφοῖς τὴν ἐπιστολὴν διαπέμψασθε, ἵνα καὶ ἐκεῖνοι δοξάζωσιν τὸν κύριον τὸν ἐκλογὰς ποιοῦντα ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων δούλων.
Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ πάντας ἡμᾶς εἰσαγαγεῖν ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ χάριτι καὶ δωρεᾷ εἰς τὴν ἐπουράνιον αὐτοῦ βασιλείαν διὰ τοῦ μονογενοῦς παιδὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δόξα, τιμή, κράτος, μεγαλωσύνη εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. προσαγορεύετε πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους. ὑμᾶς οἱ σὺν ἡμῖν προσαγορεύουσιν καὶ Εὐάρεστος ὁ γράψας πανοικεί.
orientation: The church of Smyrna is closing its letter to the church at Philomelium, asking them to forward the account and offering final praise to God.
pass_a_gloss: You then requested that the things that happened be made clear to you through more words, but we for the present have reported in summary through our brother Marcianus. Having learned these things then, send the letter also to the brothers beyond, so that they too may glorify the Lord who makes choices from his own servants. To the one who is able to bring all of us into his heavenly kingdom in his grace and gift through his only-begotten child Jesus Christ, be glory, honor, power, greatness forever. Greet all the saints. Those with us greet you, and Evaristus who wrote it, with his whole household.

choices.why: The phrase means 'by headings' or 'in summary form,' contrasting with the fuller account requested.
The phrase means brothers further on or beyond, referring to other churches beyond Philomelium.
The participle with object means 'making selections/choices,' referring to God choosing martyrs from his servants.
The term παῖς can mean 'child' or 'servant'; here with μονογενοῦς it refers to Christ as God's only-begotten child.
The adverb means 'with all his house' or 'with his entire household,' indicating Evaristus's family joined in the greeting.

pass_b_english: You asked for a fuller account of what happened, but for now we have reported it to you in summary through our brother Marcianus. Once you have learned these things, send this letter on to the brothers beyond, so that they too may glorify the Lord, who chooses from among his own servants.

To him who is able to bring us all into his heavenly kingdom through his grace and gift, through his only-begotten child Jesus Christ, be glory, honor, power, and greatness forever. Greet all the saints. Those with us greet you, and so does Evaristus, who wrote this letter, together with his whole household.

last_rejected.quote: who makes choices from among his own servants
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν ἐκλογὰς ποιοῦντα ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων δούλων
last_rejected.why: English 'choices' is weak; ἐκλογὰς means 'elections/selections' or 'chosen ones'. But 'makes choices' is within semantic range. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐκλογὰς ποιοῦντα means 'making choices/selections'; 'makes choices' is within normal semantic range.

polish.changed: Clarified the flow of the closing greetings and doxology, kept every claim and reference intact, and made the sentence rhythm more natural for reading aloud without altering the source.

notes.why: Marcianus is never identified; reader does not know his role.
notes.fix: Add brief note identifying Marcianus as the letter-carrier or correspondent.

notes.why: Evaristus appears without introduction; reader does not know his relationship to the community.
notes.fix: Note Evaristus is the scribe or secretary of the letter.
